one_liner: Sherlock (sherlock-project) is a local open-source Python CLI for username enumeration across 400+ sites. It has no hosted HTTP API or credentials, so it can't become a standard hosted-API toolkit.
auth_notes: The CLI help on the repo page lists no credential or API key options. It is a local tool with nothing to authenticate against. Other products named Sherlock (for example the Covertlabs infostealer MCP and the .NET assembly MCP) are unrelated.
access_notes: The MIT-licensed CLI is free to install (pipx, docker, dnf) and run locally. There is no vendor-hosted service to get credentials for.
blocker_notes: It is a local CLI with no hosted API. A toolkit would have to run the CLI itself, for example through a community MCP wrapper that shells out to it. The registry entry com.hostsherlock/mcp is not confirmed by any provided page, and it may belong to a different product. The mcp field is therefore kept as community, with low confidence.
